_source: Hand-verified during research: each state's own Secretary of State (or equivalent) official candidate database, checked directly (live network inspection of the real API/page, not scraped from a third party like Ballotpedia) for a machine-readable, no-key, official source that distinguishes a real confirmed general-election candidate from an FEC filer who lost their primary or runoff.
_method: A state with no entry here is simply not yet covered — the ballot page falls back to its prior behavior (every active FEC filer shown) for that state, same as any other partial-coverage feature in this app (ballot measures, county-district crosswalk). This file only ever ADDS accuracy, never removes a state's chance at showing candidates.
_discovery: This file is the HAND-VERIFIED directory, and it always wins. state_source_crawler.py also finds sources on its own each week and records what it proves in a separate discovered file, covering states nobody has written up here yet — so coverage grows, and a state that redesigns its website is re-found rather than silently broken. What the crawler will NEVER infer is the stable law in this file: a runoff threshold, a convention threshold, top-two counting. Those decide who is actually a nominee, and a state needing one must be written up here, which then overrides whatever was discovered.
_contract: Adding a state is an entry in this file, not code. Every state — however unusual — is described with the SAME keys, and a state that needs a knob nobody has needed yet gets that knob added to its adapter for everyone, never a branch on its name: there is no state code anywhere in the fetch modules. Keys, and which strategy honours them: strategy (all: tx_civix | pa_returns | clarity | tabular | canvass_xml | nj_certification | ky_certification | in_enr | tn_precinct | al_special_primary | ms_recap | ar_enr). runoff_threshold_pct (all: the state's own second-primary rule, e.g. 50 for TX/GA, 30 for NC; null where a plurality nominates). advance_count (all except canvass_xml, which is always a single-party contest by construction and has no top-two/top-four shape to advance more than one from — see canvass_xml below: how many candidates the contest sends to the general — 1 for a party primary, 2 for top-two CA/WA, 4 for AK). discovery.mode (tabular: direct_url | s3_listing | sos_api_report | landing_page, each with its own URL keys; clarity: landing_page only, for a state whose own elections.json is empty despite live results — page_url + link_regex with one capture group for the EID, as West Virginia needs) — no cycle's path is ever hardcoded. discovery.election_name_regex (tabular/sos_api_report: one pattern, or a LIST when a state decides nominees across several same-day elections like Virginia's separate D and R primaries), discovery.runoff_name_regex, discovery.report_name, discovery.require_official (withhold until the portal certifies), discovery.settle_days (release anyway once the election is this far past — the failsafe for a portal that never flips its official flag, as Utah's doesn't, and the ONLY gate for a state that publishes no flag at all, as Florida doesn't). Both gate keys apply to every discovery mode, not just the portal one. format.format/delimiter/encoding/member_regex (tabular: how to read the download — csv, tsv, xlsx, zipped). format.contest_column/choice_column/party_column/votes_column (tabular: where the four facts live; contest_column and choice_column also accept a LIST of columns to join, for a state that splits the contest across race and party columns or a name across first and last, as Florida does). format.exclude_choices (tabular: summary rows like 'Ballots Cast' that sit in the same shape as a candidate). filings (optional, any strategy: where the state's candidate FILING list lives — discovery + format, with format.election_date_column naming the column that dates each filing). It answers a different question from results, at a different time: who is on the PRIMARY ballot months before anyone votes, and when that primary is. It is strictly weaker than a confirmed nominee and never overrides one. format.house_from_columns (tabular: for a state whose office LABEL can't be trusted to identify a federal seat — names the column, the value marking a congressional seat, and the district-number column). canvass_xml (discovery.base_url with a {year} slot, discovery.keyword, discovery.report_name default 'Results.Summary.xml', discovery.settle_days): for a state whose official canvass is a single per-election XML export served over plain FTP rather than any results-platform vendor — lists the year directory, keeps the entry whose name contains keyword, and reads that election's report_name file. No 'official' flag exists in this format, so settling is judged from the file itself (statewide precinctsReportingPercent=100.00) plus the same settle_days failsafe every other vendor uses.

CO.source_name: Colorado Secretary of State (Clarity Election Night Reporting)
CO.description: Official statewide results feed, verified live 2026-08-12 against the real 2026 primary (EID 126592): elections.json -> current_ver.txt -> json/sum.json, no API key or auth. All 18 federal contests (8 districts x 2 parties, plus both Senate primaries) parse cleanly. Ground-truthed against the CO-01 Democratic primary, where the feed shows Melat Kiros 83,855 (53.2%) defeating 15-term incumbent Diana DeGette 62,715 with Wanda James third — matching what actually happened on 2026-06-30. runoff_threshold_pct is null because Colorado awards its primary to the plurality leader outright, so the top vote-getter IS the nominee; a runoff state must set this or its runoff-bound leader would be mislabeled.

IA.source_name: Iowa Secretary of State (Clarity Election Night Reporting)
IA.description: Second state on the Clarity adapter, added 2026-08-16 on a re-probe of all 50 states' Clarity feeds — Iowa had published nothing for 2026 when the same probe ran on 2026-08-12, and its 2026-06-02 primary (EID 126082) is there now, so this file's coverage grows without code as states publish. All 10 federal contests parse (4 districts x 2 parties, plus both Senate primaries). Ground-truthed on the real result: Miller-Meeks holding IA-01 against Pautsch with Bohannan again taking the Democratic side, and Ashley Hinson winning the Senate primary — which is why IA-02 is an open-seat race. runoff_threshold_pct is 35, and it is NOT a runoff rule: Iowa Code 43.52 sends a nomination to a party CONVENTION when nobody clears 35%, so a sub-threshold leader isn't merely unconfirmed, they may well not be the nominee at all. IA-04's Democratic primary is the live case — Dawson took it on 39.0% of a three-way field, close enough to that line to matter.

IL.source_name: Illinois State Board of Elections (official vote totals by office)
IL.description: Illinois posts one precinct-level CSV PER OFFICE rather than a single statewide export, so its 17 congressional files plus the Senate file are read as 18 stages off the board's own vote-totals page — which is also why the link pattern, not any one file's URL, is what's written down. '{year}GP' pins the cycle's General Primary and excludes the general election's own files. The contest label is bare ('1ST CONGRESS'), which parse_office reads as a federal seat because no state legislature is called a Congress; party lives only in its own column, so the contest key carries it, without which both parties' primaries for a district would tally as one race. Verified live 2026-08-17 against the real 2026-03-17 primary.

MD.source_name: Maryland State Board of Elections (official primary results)
MD.description: Maryland publishes results as HTML tables under headings rather than as any downloadable file, which is why the html_table reader exists — the table alone never says which contest it is, so every row carries the heading stack it appeared under and the contest is built from it ('Representative in Congress' + 'District 1'). The link pattern deliberately matches EVERY office summary page rather than pinning the congressional one's internal office number: parse_office already refuses Governor, Comptroller and the state legislature, so matching broadly costs a few extra pages and survives Maryland renumbering its offices. The party heading joins the contest key ('Democratic Candidates - Vote for 1'): without it both parties' candidates for a district tally as ONE race and, in a district that leans hard either way, the other party's nominee is dropped entirely — 8 records instead of 16. Verified live 2026-08-18 against the real 2026-06-23 primary: 92 candidate rows across all 8 districts.

MN.source_name: Minnesota Secretary of State (election night reporting files)
MN.description: Minnesota was written off twice as captcha-blocked, and the interesting part is HOW it is blocked: its bot manager challenges the SECOND request in a window, whatever client makes it — so the page listing its result files is effectively unreachable from a pipeline that also has to fetch anything else. Its FILE host is wide open and answers every time. So Minnesota is addressed directly by election date, which is known for every state from the FEC's national calendar (state_election_dates.py) — the calendar and the fetcher composing to reach a state neither could reach alone, with no browser and without touching the protected host. One semicolon-delimited file carries every race, county by county; it has NO header row, so the columns are named positionally in config. Minnesota's Democrats are the DFL, which normalize_party now reads, and its party column holds bare letter codes, read only when the whole value is the code. Verified live 2026-08-19 on the real 2026-08-11 primary: Pete Stauber taking MN-08's Republican primary with 87.29%.

AL.source_name: Alabama Secretary of State (election-night results, special primary only)
AL.description: Covers only the 4 congressional districts (1, 2, 6, 7) Alabama re-ran in a single-round SPECIAL primary on 2026-08-11 after a mid-decade court-ordered redistricting (Louisiana v. Callais) — that special primary had NO runoff by law, so a plurality nominates. The other 3 districts (3, 4, 5) and the US Senate seat were decided by the ORDINARY May 19 primary / June 16 runoff, which this entry does NOT cover: every state-certified nominee document for that cycle is a flat scanned PDF with no text layer at all (verified: pdftotext/pdffonts/pdfimages against 6 of them show zero embedded fonts, JPEG/JBIG2 images only), and the one piece that would let results-derivation close the gap without OCR — the Republican Senate runoff's own vote count — has no published machine-readable file anywhere found; the Democratic runoff's Excel export is public, the Republican Party's apparently was shared with the Secretary of State's office directly rather than posted. Those 3 districts and the Senate seat keep the ordinary FEC-filer fallback rather than being guessed from news coverage of the certification. See state_candidates_al.py's own docstring for the full source hunt and the ecode-permanence verification. Verified live 2026-09-03: Jerry Carl CD1 (R, 74.70%), Rhett Marques CD2 (R, 50.03%), Maurice Mercer CD6 (D, 64.17%), Gary Palmer CD6 (R, 86.98%), Ammie Akin CD7 (R, 73.37%).

MS.source_name: Mississippi Secretary of State (Official Recapitulation PDF)
MS.description: The SOS's own per-party 'Official Recapitulation' PDF, discovered fresh every run through 3 real hops (the stable election-results index page -> that cycle's own results page, matched by its constant '-{party}-primary-results' suffix, never a templated slug -> the iframe it embeds -> the statewide PDF link on that iframe page), all plain server-rendered HTML, no JS needed. Reached with BROWSER_HEADERS with no bot-detection friction (a bare header set gets an Akamai 'Access Denied', same shape as OH/MO/TN/NY/GA/MN). The PDF itself (ActiveReports-generated, real embedded text, not scanned) prints one row per candidate and one column per county, sliding across as many pages as it takes to cover all 82 -- a candidate's real total is only complete on the LAST page their row appears on, which state_candidates_ms.py resolves with a running {name: total} map overwritten on every occurrence, needing no per-page 'is this the final one' detection. Mississippi nominates on a MAJORITY (Miss. Const. of 1890's primary-runoff requirement) -- runoff_threshold_pct is 50, though every real 2026 federal contest in both parties cleared it on the first round (closest: Republican CD2 at 51.1%), so the 2026-04-07 runoff decided no federal race and this entry reads only the primary PDFs. Verified live 2026-09-04 against the real, certified 2026-03-10 primary: Cindy Hyde-Smith (Senate R, incumbent), Scott Colom (Senate D), Trent Kelly (CD1 R, incumbent), Cliff Johnson (CD1 D), Ron Eller (CD2 R), Bennie Thompson (CD2 D, incumbent), Michael Guest (CD3 R, incumbent), Michael Chiaradio (CD3 D), Mike Ezell (CD4 R, incumbent), Jeffrey Hulum III (CD4 D) -- the last a real late-qualified candidate the Democratic PDF appends in his own trailing block with no repeated contest header, correctly inheriting CD4 from the last header seen before his block starts.

AK.source_name: Alaska Division of Elections (election night precinct CSV)
AK.description: Alaska runs a NONPARTISAN TOP-FOUR primary, so advance_count is 4 and every candidate is in one contest regardless of party — the same structural fork California and Washington's top-two introduced, one step wider. Its results are one precinct-level CSV per election, linked from the division's own results page (the 'enr26' path segment is per-cycle, so the pattern is what's written down, never the URL). Names are printed FEC-style, 'Darden, Dustin Thomas House', where the surname is everything before the comma and the trailing token is a middle name — hence name_format. Alaska's file is election-night data with no certification flag, and its date comes from the national calendar, so it withholds until 21 days past the primary. Verified live 2026-08-19: both federal contests present, 28,455 precinct rows.

HI.source_name: Hawaii Office of Elections (statewide summary file)
HI.description: Hawaii publishes one tab-delimited summary per election, opening with a '#FormatVersion' banner before the header row (hence skip_lines). It numbers congressional districts in ROMAN numerals — 'U.S. Representative, Dist I' — which parse_office now reads, bounded to I-XX. Its party lives on the CONTEST ('N' nonpartisan, 'D', 'R', 'G'), so the contest key carries it and the nonpartisan races are skipped for having no party at all. Names are 'CASE, Ed', surname before the comma. The file carries no date, so its date comes from the national calendar and it withholds until 21 days past the primary.

CA.source_name: California Secretary of State (certified Statement of Vote)
CA.description: Certified Statement of Vote workbook for voter-nominated (top-two) offices, verified live 2026-08-15: county-level rows carrying Contest Name ('United States Representative District 10'), Candidate Name, Party Name and Vote Total, read with the standard library since an xlsx is a zip of XML and no Excel dependency is warranted. All 52 congressional districts are present; California has no Senate seat on the 2026 ballot. advance_count is 2 because California runs a single all-party primary and sends the TOP TWO to the general regardless of party — modelling it as one nominee per party would silently drop a real ballot option, including the same-party runoffs California regularly produces. runoff_threshold_pct is null: there is no runoff, the top two simply advance.

WA.source_name: Washington Secretary of State (official results portal)
WA.description: Same portal software as Georgia's, reached through the identical sos_api_report discovery — which is the whole point of the vendor-adapter split: Washington cost a config entry, not a module. Verified live 2026-08-15 (publicElectionId 20260804, 'U.S. Representative - Congressional District N', 976 rows). advance_count is 2: Washington is a top-two state like California, and its party column is free-text candidate PREFERENCE ('Prefers Cascade Democrat Party', 'Prefers No Kings Party'), which is only ever a tiebreak here, never the match signal. require_official is set because Washington votes by mail and was still counting on 2026-08-15 — isOfficialResults was false, so this state correctly confirms nobody until certification on 2026-08-18, then lights up on its own. settle_days is the failsafe under that gate: Utah proved the portal's official flag is not reliably flipped, so a certified-but-unflagged election still counts once it is 30 days past. No Washington Senate seat is on the 2026 ballot.

VA.source_name: Virginia Department of Elections (official results portal)
VA.description: Third state on the same Enhanced Voting portal as Georgia and Washington, so again a config entry rather than a module. Two things make Virginia different, and both are why it waited: it runs its Democratic and Republican primaries as two SEPARATE elections on the same day (publicElectionIds 2026-August-Democratic-Primary and 2026-August-Republican-Primary, both 2026-08-04), hence a list of election patterns; and its federal label is 'Member, House of Representatives (2nd District)' with no 'U.S.' prefix, which parse_office deliberately refuses so a state lower chamber can't slip through — the export's own DistrictType == 'congressional' column is the discriminator instead. Verified live 2026-08-16 against the real CSVs: Elaine Luria taking the VA-02 Democratic primary, Don Beyer VA-08, Tom Perriello VA-05. Virginia nominates on a plurality, so there is no runoff threshold. require_official is set and both primaries were still uncertified 12 days out, so Virginia confirms nobody until the state board certifies, then lights up on its own — or, under settle_days, 30 days out if this portal never flips its official flag (Utah's never did). Only contested races appear in these files — an unopposed nominee is simply absent, and that seat keeps the FEC-filer fallback.

FL.source_name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections (election night results file)
FL.description: Florida's own election-night file, one tab-delimited row per candidate per county, verified 2026-08-16 against the real 2024-08-20 primary (Republican Senate primary: Rick Scott 1,081,109 over three challengers) and against the 2026-08-18 file the state had already staged, zeroed, before polls opened. The URL carries the election DATE, so it is read off the state's own downloads page each run rather than written down here — and a file dated on the cycle's federal election day is skipped, because that one is the GENERAL, whose results can't confirm a nominee for the race they decide. Florida splits across columns what other states keep in one label: the contest is (RaceName, PartyCode) — without the party code both parties' primaries for a seat would tally as ONE race and the bigger primary would 'win' the seat outright — and the candidate is (CanNameFirst, CanNameLast). RaceName reads 'Representative in Congress, District 2', which parse_office rightly refuses, so RaceCode == 'USR' identifies the House seat and Juris1num carries the number. Florida abolished its primary runoff in 2002, so a plurality nominates and there is no threshold. It publishes no certification flag anywhere in this file — it starts filling with partial counts the moment polls close — so settle_days is the ONLY gate here, and Florida names nobody until 21 days past its primary.

UT.source_name: Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office (official results portal)
UT.description: Fourth state on the Enhanced Voting portal, found on 2026-08-16 by probing /results/public/ across state results hosts — pure config, no code. Verified live against the real 2026-06-23 primary workbook: Ben McAdams taking the UT-01 Democratic primary, Blake Moore UT-02 and Celeste Maloy UT-03 on the Republican side (district numbers are the post-2026-redistricting map, which is exactly why they come from the state's own feed rather than being inferred). Only 3 federal contests exist — Utah's convention/signature path means most seats never reach a primary ballot, and an unopposed nominee is simply absent here. The name pattern excludes Utah's odd-year MUNICIPAL primary. Utah is why settle_days exists: this primary was canvassed and certified on 2026-07-22, its signed state canvass report is published on this very portal, and isOfficialResults was STILL false a month later — so require_official alone would have confirmed nobody here forever.

GA.source_name: Georgia Secretary of State (official results portal)
GA.description: Official statewide totals workbook, discovered live 2026-08-15 through the portal's own API rather than any hardcoded path: jurisdictions/Georgia lists every election (publicElectionId 'GeneralPrimary51926' for the 2026-05-19 General Primary) plus the portal id, the election document names its report blobs, and the blob GUID — which changes on every republish — is read each run. 30 federal contests. Georgia nominates on a majority, so runoff_threshold_pct is 50 AND the 2026-06-16 General Primary Runoff is fetched as a second stage that overrides the primary for every race it decides; without that merge the runoff seats would stay permanently unconfirmed. exclude_choices drops the per-contest 'Total Votes' summary row, which sits in the same shape as a candidate and would otherwise double the denominator and win uncontested races outright.

NM.source_name: New Mexico Secretary of State (official election results portal)
NM.description: Statewide CSV export off the SOS's own ASP.NET results portal (electionresults.sos.nm.gov), reached with no login, no session and no bot-detection friction — verified both via a real browser session and a plain unauthenticated server-side fetch on 2026-09-03. The URL carries no election id or date: it always serves whichever election is currently featured, which is exactly what makes it safe to leave unhardcoded across cycles. type=FED already scopes the export to the state's 4 federal contests (Senate + 3 House districts), so nothing else needs filtering out. RaceName alone doesn't carry the House district ('United States Representative', no number) — AreaNum does ('DISTRICT 1') — nor does either column carry the party on its own, so the contest key joins all three; without PartyCode a district's Democratic and Republican primaries would tally as ONE race and only the higher-turnout party's candidate would ever be picked (New Mexico's real 2026 primary had 574k Democratic ballots against 444k Republican, so every Republican nominee would have been silently dropped). Joining AreaNum in is also what lets parse_office's own District-number matching resolve the seat with no house_from_columns spec needed. The file carries no date or certification flag of its own, so held comes from the national FEC calendar (date_from_calendar) and require_official/settle_days gate on that: New Mexico is a runoff-free plurality state (NM Const. art. VII § 5; primary runoffs are constitutionally barred) and certified this cycle's primary in exactly 21 days (held 2026-06-02, State Canvass Board certification 2026-06-23), so settle_days matches the state's own real turnaround. Verified live against the certified 2026-06-02 primary: Ben Ray Lujan's Senate renomination, and Melanie Stansbury (NM-01), Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) and Teresa Leger Fernandez (NM-03) each renominated on the Democratic side, plus a Republican Senate write-in nominee (surname parsing strips the '(write in)' annotation the same way Georgia's incumbency markers are stripped).

NC.source_name: North Carolina State Board of Elections (public results export)
NC.description: Official statewide precinct-results export, verified live 2026-08-12 against the real 2026-03-03 primary: the S3 listing at dl.ncsbe.gov resolves ENRS/2026 -> results_pct_20260303.zip (1.4 MB, 103,517 rows, 49,884 federal) with no key or auth, yielding 21 federal contests. Ground-truthed on Virginia Foxx taking NC-05 Republican with 74.5% and Valerie Foushee NC-04 Democratic with 49.2%. runoff_threshold_pct is 30 because North Carolina nominates on 30%+1 and sends anything below to a second primary — NC-01 Republican was won on 39.5%, which clears it, but a sub-30% leader must not be confirmed while a second primary is still possible.

filings.description: Who is on the ballot — BOTH ballots — months before any result exists, plus the primary's own date. Verified live 2026-08-17 against the real file (8,300 rows, one per county per candidate; 71 federal primary candidates dated 03/03/2026, and 42 on the general ballot dated 11/03/2026). The general list is why this matters beyond the pre-primary window: 15 of those 42 are Libertarian or Green candidates who never appear in ANY primary, so confirming nominees from primary results cannot see them — and since a race with any confirmed candidate shows only confirmed candidates, they were being dropped from the page. North Carolina records the primary a candidate ran in (party_contest, empty for November) separately from the candidate's own party (party_candidate, which is where LIB/GRE appear), hence both columns. Only office, ballot name, party and election date are read: the same file also carries every candidate's home address, phone and email, which this platform has no reason to hold. general_ballot_complete is set on this state because these general-ballot rows ARE the November ballot, minor parties included.

PA.description: Pennsylvania looked unreachable for months because electionreturns.pa.gov's front page sits behind Imperva and answers a bot challenge — but its API does not, and serves a plain server-side request fine. The endpoints were read off the page's own network activity in a browser on 2026-08-18 and then confirmed with no browser involved. Election and office are matched by CODE, never wording: ElectionType 'P' is the general primary, OfficeCode 'USC'/'USS' the federal offices, so the ids (117 for 2026) never need writing down. Verified live against the real 2026-05-19 primary: Bob Harvie taking PA-01's Democratic primary with 65.14%. Pennsylvania has no Senate seat on the 2026 ballot and nominates on a plurality, so there is no runoff threshold.

TX.source_name: Texas Secretary of State (Civix Candidate Bio Portal)
TX.description: Official statewide candidate database, verified live via network inspection (not scraping the rendered Angular SPA): GET .../getElectionsByYear/{year} to find the current cycle's 'GE' (General Election) id, then POST .../findQualifiedCandidates with that id. cdOfficeType='FD' isolates federal races; txOfficeName parses to office+district ('U. S. SENATOR' / 'U. S. REPRESENTATIVE DISTRICT N'); cdFilingStatus='CG' ('Candidate in the General Election') is the authoritative confirmed-nominee flag, verified against known-correct 2026 ground truth (Paxton beat Cornyn in the May runoff; Paxton alone carries CG, Cornyn is absent from the GE-scoped query entirely). No API key, no auth. general_ballot_complete: Civix reports the state's own general-election FILING STATUS, so this list is the whole November ballot rather than the major-party nominees — live 2026-08-17 it carries 5 Green, 3 Libertarian and 1 independent candidate alongside the 39 Democrats and 39 Republicans.

AZ.source_name: Arizona Secretary of State (statewide canvass XML, FTP)
AZ.description: Found specifically because azsos.gov's own website sits behind Cloudflare bot-detection this codebase won't attempt to defeat — the FTP host serving the SAME official canvass was never protected at all, same 'the listing page is guarded but its file host isn't' shape as Minnesota's adapter. Verified live 2026-09-02 against the real, certified 2026 primary (resultsTimestamp 2026-08-05, 100% of 1,786 precincts reporting): all 9 congressional districts present with real multi-candidate fields, third parties (LBT/GRN) included in the source data though normalize_party only recognises Libertarian/Green, not AZ's standalone No Labels party (NOL), which is correctly skipped rather than guessed at. runoff_threshold_pct is null because Arizona's runoff law was repealed in 1992 — federal primaries are decided by plurality, same as CA/CO/WA's top-line rule. No U.S. Senate contest appears in the 2026 primary file at all — not verified against Arizona's own Senate-seat-class calendar, so this is read as "none this cycle" rather than assumed; if one appears in a later cycle's file it needs no code change, since parse_office already recognises a Senate label on sight.

NJ.source_name: New Jersey Division of Elections (Certification of General Election Nominees)
NJ.description: A different shape entirely from every other state on file: New Jersey has no primary-runner-up problem to solve, because it never nominates through a scraped results feed at all — the Division of Elections itself publishes the state's own POST-primary confirmed slate as a single PDF, one evergreen URL pattern per year (nj.gov/state/elections/assets/pdf/election-results/{year}/{year}-certification-of-general-election-nominees_us-senate_us-house.pdf), verified live 2026-09-03 against the real document (dated 07/27/2026, 'For GENERAL ELECTION 11/03/2026') and confirmed as the same pattern that resolved for the real 2024 cycle too. general_ballot_complete is deliberately NOT set: although this certification lists the state's real minor-party nominees (District 3's Green candidate Welzer IS captured), the parser only recognizes party text that normalize_party already knows (Democratic/Republican/Libertarian/Green) and correctly refuses to guess at anything else — a real independent or minor-slogan candidate (verified live in District 8: 'INDEPENDENT', 'SOCIALIST WORKERS PARTY', 'WE THE PEOPLE') is silently absent from the parsed list even though they ARE on the real November ballot, so this source is real but incomplete in the same way a primary-results state is, and candidateSource must say 'nominees', not 'confirmed'. No discovery block is needed: unlike a results vendor, this PDF is filed at a fixed, predictable URL the moment the state certifies, so there is no election id or blob GUID to resolve first. It is a genuinely column-based tabular report rather than narrative text, parsed by each row's word x0 position (Name x0<130, Party 260<=x0<320) rather than by regex over flowing text, because an independent candidate's own free-text slogan repeats in ALL CAPS on county-repeat rows in a way that defeats a casing-based heuristic. runoff_threshold_pct is null because this document lists confirmed NOMINEES directly; there is no primary-vote-share threshold for this strategy to apply.

KY.source_name: Kentucky State Board of Elections (Primary Certification of Vote Totals)
KY.description: The State Board of Elections' own certified, county-by-county vote-total PDF for the primary — genuinely different in shape from every other state on file: a candidate is a COLUMN and a county is a ROW, sometimes printed with the candidate's name rotated 90 degrees to fit a crowded field into narrow columns (the real 2026 US Senate Republican primary had 11 candidates). Verified live 2026-09-03 against the real 2026 document (44 pages, certified 2026-06-01): all 11 of the cycle's federal contests resolved cleanly (Senate + 6 House districts across both parties where contested), each cross-checked against the document's own printed county-level tallies. Neither the results FILE's directory nor its filename is stable across cycles — 2024's file lived at /results/2020-2029/Documents/2024 Primary Results.pdf, 2026's at /Documents/2026 Primary Certification of Vote Totals Final.pdf, a different name AND a different directory — so both are read off each year's own results page (the module's own DISCOVERY constant captures whatever directory segment precedes the filename, rather than assuming one). Every candidate column's surname is read by clustering that page's words to the NEAREST vote-total column by word CENTER (not left edge — a long name like the real hyphenated surname PERRY-ADELMANN starts far enough left of a narrow column that left-edge matching pulled it into the wrong candidate's cluster) and then trusting only the cluster's single ALL-CAPS word (Mc/Mac surnames like the real McGRATH keep their natural lowercase second letter even in this all-caps header style, and are matched as such), which held constant across every real case examined regardless of given-name word count or rotation. Never guessed: any column whose cluster doesn't resolve to exactly one such surname skips the whole contest rather than risk attributing real votes to the wrong name — not yet exercised by the real document itself, only by a constructed test case, since every real 2026 contest resolved unambiguously. Kentucky nominates on a plain plurality with no runoff or convention threshold, so runoff_threshold_pct is null.

IN.description: Indiana's own election-night-reporting site, found by driving it in a browser and reading its own network calls: data/settings.json carries a Certified flag (gates everything, same role as require_official elsewhere) and a short VersionType cache-busting tag every other file's name is suffixed with; data/statewideElectionsC_{version}.json is the FULL office manifest grouped by heading, read fresh every run to find the Federal category's OFFICECATEGORYID (never hardcoded — verified live 2026-09-03 that Indiana's real 2026 manifest lists exactly one Federal category, 'US Representative', and no Senate category, meaning Indiana has no Senate seat up this cycle; a future cycle needing one adds no code, since a second Federal manifest entry is picked up automatically). Each race's district is read from its own SubSortOrder numeric code ('...(1) District'), not OFFICE_TITLE's spelled-out ordinal word, for the same evergreen-over-wording reason PA matches by code. Each candidate carries both Indiana's own isWinner flag AND a raw vote total; isWinner is NOT trusted directly (it showed no visible tie-handling of its own during review) — the vote totals are run through the same shared, tie-safe pick_nominee every vote-count-based strategy uses, and its answer matched isWinner exactly on the real, certified 2026 primary (WriteTime 2026-08-20): all 9 US House districts resolved, including a real 11-candidate District 4 field where only the 2 genuine winners (one per party) were kept. runoff_threshold_pct is null: Indiana nominates on a plain plurality.

TN.source_name: Tennessee Secretary of State (statewide precinct-level results workbook)
TN.description: sos.tn.gov itself sits behind Cloudflare and answers a bot challenge to a bare request, but the SAME browser-header approach that already unblocked OH/MO/TN/NY/GA/MN (see http_utils.BROWSER_HEADERS) answers it fine, and the actual FILE host (sos-prod.tnsosgovfiles.com) was never protected at all. A genuinely different SHAPE from every other tabular state, hence its own module rather than a tabular config entry: Tennessee publishes one row per PRECINCT per office per party (roughly 40,000 rows for the whole state), with up to 5 candidates packed sideways into repeated column groups (RNAME1/PARTY1/PVTALLY1 .. RNAME5/PARTY5/PVTALLY5) rather than one row per candidate — a statewide total means summing the same candidate's tally across every precinct row, which the tabular format's column-mapping has no way to express. Discovery reuses tabular's own landing_page mode unchanged (state_candidates_tabular._discover_urls): the results page lists every past election's files, each dated in its own filename ('20260806AllbyPrecinct.xlsx'), the same shape Florida's discovery already handles. runoff_threshold_pct is 50, and it is a REAL, load-bearing state law, not a tuning knob: Tenn. Code Ann. 2-8-113 sends any federal primary that fails to clear a majority to a runoff on the last Thursday in August, and pick_nominee's own withholding is what keeps a runoff-bound plurality leader from being mislabeled the nominee — verified live against the real 2026 primary, where 6 of 18 federal party fields (real 3+-way splits) came in under 50% and are correctly left unconfirmed. Tennessee publishes no certification flag anywhere in this file (same as Florida), so require_official is set purely to switch discovery's settle_days gate on, which is the only thing judging freshness here.

WV.source_name: West Virginia Secretary of State (Clarity Election Night Reporting)
WV.description: Fifth state on the Clarity adapter, and the first that needed a real change to the shared module rather than just a config entry: West Virginia's own copy of /WV/elections.json — the endpoint every other Clarity state's EID discovery reads — is empty, even though its real, live 2026 results are reachable at a specific election id. The state's own elections page (sos.wv.gov/elections) keeps a current link to that id, so this entry adds a new, general `discovery: {mode: landing_page}` capability to state_candidates_clarity.py itself (available to any future Clarity state in the same situation, not a West-Virginia-specific branch) — the same 'the listing endpoint is empty/blocked but a static page still points at the real data' shape Minnesota's and Arizona's adapters already handle for their own vendors. Verified live 2026-09-03 against the real, certified 2026 primary (EID 126209): both federal contests resolved — US Senate (a real 6-candidate Republican field, Shelley Moore Capito winning outright; a real 5-candidate Democratic field, Rachel Fetty Anderson winning) and both US House districts, both parties. West Virginia nominates by plain plurality with no runoff (W. Va. Code 3-5-4(b)), so runoff_threshold_pct is null.

AR.source_name: Arkansas Secretary of State (Tally ENR election-night results)
AR.description: The SOS's own election-night-reporting vendor (totalresults.com's "Tally ENR", enr-results-api.totalresults.com), a clean multi-endpoint REST JSON API keyed by cid=arkansas and per-election GUIDs discovered fresh every run (GetElectionList matched by electionName -- "Preferential Primary" for the first round, "Primary Runoff" for the second -- and electionDate's year, never a hardcoded election id). No login, no session, no bot-detection friction at all: a plain unauthenticated GET succeeds. Party is a literal prefix on the contest name itself ("REP U.S. Senate", "DEM U.S. Congress District 02"), and only a CONTESTED race gets its own contest entry -- Arkansas's real 2026 CD1, CD3 and the CD4 Republican side were all unopposed and simply absent from the feed, correctly left to the ordinary FEC-filer fallback. Arkansas nominates on a MAJORITY (Ark. Code Ann. Sec 7-7-407); runoff_threshold_pct is 50, though every real 2026 federal contest cleared it in the first round (closest: the DEM CD4 primary at 53%), so state_candidates_ar.py's runoff-stage fetch -- which DOES merge in a runoff's results over the primary's for any seat that needs it -- is proven live to safely no-op this cycle, not just written and untested. Verified live 2026-09-04 against the real, certified 2026-03-03 primary: Tom Cotton (Senate R, incumbent, 82%), Hallie Shoffner (Senate D, 78%), French Hill (CD2 R, incumbent, 77%), Chris Jones (CD2 D, 93%), James "Rus" Russell III (CD4 D, 53%).

_dates: A state's primary DATE is read off the same feed its results come from and cached in state_election_dates.json (see state_election_dates.py) — never a calendar anybody maintains here. The November general is statutory and computed instead (election_calendar.py). A state with no registered source has no known primary date, and says so rather than guessing.
_ballot_completeness: KNOWN GAP, by source kind. A state confirmed from primary RESULTS can only ever show people who ran in a primary — Libertarian, Green and independent candidates reach November without one, so they are invisible to it, and because a race with any confirmed candidate shows only confirmed candidates, they are dropped from the page rather than merely unmarked. Two source kinds do not have this problem and prove the point: TEXAS confirms from the state's general-election FILING STATUS, and its 88 confirmed candidates include 5 Green, 3 Libertarian and 1 independent; NORTH CAROLINA now reads its filing list's general-ballot rows, which carry 10 Libertarians and 2 Greens the primary results never mentioned. The remaining results-only states (CA, CO, FL, GA, IA, UT, VA, WA) show nominees only until a filing list or general-ballot source is registered for them. Adding one is a `filings` block, not code.
